intitule: Exercise 1: Identifying Formal and Informal Registers

enonce.texte:
Identify whether each sentence is formal or informal.

Write 'F' for formal and 'I' for informal.

questions.texte: 'Hey, how's it going?'
questions.reponse: I

questions.texte: 'Good morning, how are you today?'
questions.reponse: F

questions.texte: 'I'd like to introduce myself. My name is John.'
questions.reponse: F

questions.texte: 'Nice to meet you, I'm John.'
questions.reponse: I

questions.texte: 'Could you please send me the report by Friday?'
questions.reponse: F

enonce.texte:
Write a professional introduction for a networking event.

Include: your name, job title, company, and one interesting fact about yourself.

questions.texte: Write a 30-second professional introduction.
questions.reponse: Example answer: Good evening, everyone. My name is Marie, and I am a Marketing Manager at GlobeCom. I have been working in digital marketing for five years. I am passionate about helping businesses grow their online presence. In my free time, I love photography.

enonce.texte: Match the small talk question to its appropriate context.

questions.texte: What do you do for a living?
questions.reponse: Asking about someone's job

questions.texte: How was your weekend?
questions.reponse: Asking about recent activities

questions.texte: Have you been to this conference before?
questions.reponse: Asking about previous experience

questions.texte: What brings you here today?
questions.reponse: Asking about purpose of attendance

enonce.texte:
Read the scenario and write a response.

Scenario: You are at a business conference. You see someone standing alone. You want to start a conversation and build rapport.

questions.texte: Write what you would say to start the conversation.
questions.reponse: Example answer: 'Hello, I don't think we've met. My name is Jean. I'm a software developer. Are you enjoying the conference so far?'

questions.texte: Write a follow-up question to keep the conversation going.
questions.reponse: Example answer: 'What session have you found most interesting today?'

enonce.texte: Transform the informal introduction into a formal one.

questions.texte: Informal: 'Hi, I'm Sara. Nice to meet you.'
questions.reponse: Formal: 'Good morning, my name is Sara. It's a pleasure to meet you.'

questions.texte: Informal: 'Hey, this is my boss, Mr. Smith.'
questions.reponse: Formal: 'May I introduce you to my manager, Mr. Smith?'

enonce.texte:
You are attending a professional networking event. You have 5 minutes to connect with a potential client.

Write a dialogue between you and the client. Include: introduction, small talk, building rapport, and a follow-up plan.

questions.texte: Write the dialogue.
questions.reponse: Example answer: You: 'Good evening, my name is Pierre. I'm a business consultant at Growth Solutions. I noticed you're in the technology industry.' Client: 'Yes, I'm Marie, the CEO of TechWave. It's my first time at this event.' You: 'How are you finding it so far?' Client: 'I've met some interesting people.' You: 'I'm glad to hear that. I've been working with tech companies to improve their operations. What challenges is TechWave currently facing?' Client: 'We're struggling with scaling our operations.' You: 'That's a common challenge. I'd love to discuss this further. Could we exchange cards and schedule a meeting?' Client: 'That sounds great.' You: 'I'll send you an email tomorrow to set something up.'

intitule: Exercise 7: Following Up After a Meeting

enonce.texte:
Write a follow-up email after a professional meeting.

Include: a thank you, a summary of the meeting, and a call to action.

questions.texte: Write the follow-up email.
questions.reponse: Example answer: Subject: Thank you for the meeting. Dear Mr. Smith, Thank you for taking the time to meet with me yesterday. I enjoyed learning more about your company's plans for expansion. As we discussed, I will send you a proposal outlining how our services can support your growth. Please let me know if you have any questions. I look forward to working with you. Best regards, Jean.

intitule: Exercise 8: Appropriate Register in Different Situations

enonce.texte: Choose the most appropriate response for each situation.

questions.texte: You meet your CEO at a company event.
questions.reponse: 'Good evening, Mr. CEO. It's an honor to meet you. I'm a project manager in the IT department.'

questions.texte: You meet a new colleague for the first time.
questions.reponse: 'Hello, I'm Sarah. I'm the new marketing specialist. It's great to finally meet you.'

questions.texte: You meet a friend at a social event.
questions.reponse: 'Hey! How have you been? It's been so long!'

intitule: Exercise 9: Small Talk and Building Rapport

enonce.texte: Read the following situations and write a response that builds rapport.

questions.texte: Your colleague looks stressed. You want to show empathy.
questions.reponse: 'You look like you have a lot on your plate. Is there anything I can do to help?'

questions.texte: Your client mentions they love traveling.
questions.reponse: 'That's wonderful! I love traveling too. What's your favorite destination?'

questions.texte: Your coworker shares a personal achievement.
questions.reponse: 'Congratulations! That's a fantastic achievement. You should be very proud.'

enonce.texte:
You attended a networking event and met several potential clients and partners.

Write follow-up messages for each person. Use different registers (formal, semi-formal, informal) depending on the context.

Context:

  • Person A: CEO of a large corporation (very formal)
  • Person B: Senior manager at a mid-sized company (semi-formal)
  • Person C: Freelancer you connected with (informal)

questions.texte: Write the follow-up messages for Person A, B, and C.
questions.reponse: Example answer: Person A: 'Dear Mr. CEO, It was a pleasure meeting you at the networking event. I was inspired by your talk on innovation. I would like to explore potential collaboration opportunities between our organizations. I will call your office next week to schedule a meeting. Yours sincerely, Jean.' Person B: 'Dear Mrs. Manager, It was great meeting you at the event. I enjoyed our discussion about market trends. I would love to continue the conversation and share some ideas. I will send you a calendar invitation for a brief call next week. Best regards, Jean.' Person C: 'Hey! It was awesome meeting you last night. I really enjoyed chatting about freelance projects. Let's grab coffee sometime and brainstorm ideas. Let me know when you're free! Cheers, Jean.'
